source.publication: Nick Ramsey, Geometric and p-adic Modular Forms of Half-Integral Weight, Annales de l’Institut Fourier 56(3) (2006), 599–624

old_inventory_match: A031 source family has algebraic-model locators only; this is a new exact source/occurrence link, not a manuscript repair.

obligations.source_hypotheses: Theorem 6.2 requires F in M_(k/2)(4N,R,chi), a prime l not dividing 4N, and 4Nl invertible in R. Take k=3, characteristic-zero coefficient field, l=p outside actual level support S1.
obligations.constructed_objects: The actual sieved algebraic even form of ex:app-even-phase, with scalar character psi and good eigenvalue eta(p)a_p(E).
obligations.domain_and_index_coverage: The theorem gives every Fourier index n. It includes the Legendre value zero when p divides n; a_(n/p²) is zero for a nonintegral index. No squarefree restriction.
obligations.transition_and_comparison_maps: Use the source normalized Hecke operator l^-2 pi1_*(pi2^*F times Theta_(l²)^k). Its theorem explicitly identifies this with the classical Fourier operator. No use of its bad-prime U_l or Gauss normalization.
obligations.consumed_object_identity: The source q-expansion belongs to T_(p²) of the same F. Good-Hecke eigenspace and commuting sieve give T_(p²)F=eta(p)a_p(E)F. Rearranging the coefficient equality gives E.12 for the same a(n).
obligations.coefficient_and_normalization: At k=3 the source l^((k-1)/2-1)=1 and (-1/l)^((k-1)/2)(n/l)=(-n/l). The last coefficient is p psi(p²)=p eta(p)². No conjugation or absolute square.
obligations.local_conditions: p avoids S1=S0 union B; no condition at bad or dyadic primes is inferred. The ring is a field of characteristic zero, not a residue coefficient ring.
obligations.exceptional_cases: p is odd because 2 divides the level. Terms for p dividing n and p² dividing n are part of the stated formula. Zero coefficients are allowed.
obligations.downstream_consumption: Integer shell polynomials at13693–13721, minimum-depth coefficients, O.9/O.10 divisions, and the nonempty-seed coefficient computation use this exact recurrence.
